concise_summary: Nifty Pharma hit a record high in mid-July
Novo Nordisk's India Wegovy approval hit sentiment
Trump announced a phased tariff plan on generics
Sector fell sharply on the tariff-plan announcement
Tariffs start only 2028, giving a transition window
Dr Reddy's flagged a semaglutide manufacturing issue
Q1 FY27 earnings season ran through July
Sun Pharma profit rose but missed estimates
US revenue exposure varied sharply across companies
sector_news_last_month: Nifty Pharma touched a fresh record high around mid-July, extending a rally of roughly 17% over the preceding six months
Sentiment turned cautious around the same period after a global pharma major received Indian regulatory approval for its obesity drug, raising competitive-threat concerns for some domestic players
The sector staged a sharp rebound rally shortly after, led by several mid-cap and large-cap names, comfortably outperforming the broader market on that session

Later in the month, US President Donald Trump announced a phased tariff plan for imported generic medicines: zero tariff continuing for two years from 1 August 2026, followed by a steep escalation in subsequent years
The announcement triggered a broad sector-wide selloff, with most index constituents trading lower and pharma among the weakest-performing sectors on the day

A leading domestic brokerage said the tariff plan was unlikely to have an immediate earnings impact, since the structure only begins in 2028, giving companies roughly a two-year window to diversify export markets and adjust strategy

Analyst research highlighted wide variation in individual companies' US revenue exposure, with some names having sharply reduced their US dependence in recent years while others remain far more exposed
Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) earnings season ran through the month for most major pharma companies, with a heavy cluster of results announced in the back half of July

Results were broadly mixed: strong profit growth was reported by some large-caps, though revenue and profit came in below Street estimates for at least one major player, largely due to continued weakness in its US generics business

One major company disclosed a product-quality issue affecting a key metabolic-disease drug, delaying commercial supply while the root cause is investigated, though the company said there was no patient-safety impact

A mid-cap CDMO-focused player continued an exceptionally strong multi-month rally through the period, briefly surpassing a much larger peer's market value on accelerating contract-manufacturing demand
Pipeline and regulatory newsflow continued alongside the earnings and tariff headlines, including a new late-stage clinical trial approval for a rare-disease therapy at one company
By the final week of the month, the sector showed signs of stabilising and partially recovering some of the tariff-driven losses, though trading remained more volatile than earlier in July
